title: ACR feedback a necessity
full_text:
The SMSF Association has called for more clarity from the ATO on what action it is taking when an auditor contravention report (ACR) is filed by an auditor, as well as suggesting an increase in the materiality thresholds that apply.
The professional body made the recommendations in a submission to the Australian National Audit Office (ANAO) performance audit of the ATO’s regulation of SMSFs, where it noted the importance of the ACR framework in providing information about prescribed contraventions, but requested feedback be provided to auditors.
“The association is concerned that the ATO can place undue weight on report volumes and auditor behaviour without providing feedback to improve the quality of the source data,” the submission stated.
“Members report they generally receive no feedback on whether an ACR led to action, whether the ATO considered the matter low risk or whether reporting practice is over or under calibrated.
“This makes it difficult for auditors to learn from regulatory outcomes and for the ATO to improve the consistency of the dataset it relies on.”
As such, it recommended the publication of aggregate ACR outcome information with examples of reporting that was useful, unnecessary or commonly misunderstood.
The submission also noted a large proportion of audit findings related to administrative matters, which may not be indicators of deliberate misuse or member harm, and recommended the ANAO examine how the ATO distinguishes between these matters and substantive risks when analysing ACR data.
“The ATO confirmed the increase in ACR numbers has been driven mainly by administrative breaches, including trustees failing to report assets at market value, failing to retain trustee minutes and trustees not signing declarations, rather than growth in serious contraventions,” it said.
“Over-reporting risks creating junk data, which can detract from more serious compliance matters. Reporting must be balanced with the value and best-case use of the data reported, alongside the compliance risks to SMSF auditors who do not maintain high levels of ACR lodgements versus any real high-risk activities or compliance concerns identified and acted upon by the commissioner.”
The relatively low and fixed levels of the materiality thresholds were also flagged as a problem, with the association noting reporting criteria required an ACR to be lodged where the total value of all contraventions in a fund exceeds $30,000, while if a fund was less than 15 months old, any contravention over $2000 must be reported. These figures were set in 2013 and 2011, respectively.
“A static nominal threshold can become progressively less meaningful as fund values, asset prices and the value of the penalty unit change. It can also cause breaches with very different risk characteristics to generate the same reporting obligations,” the submission said.
author: Jason Spits
heading: Superannuation and Investments
